title: Towards Early and Accurate Disease Detection Through Multimodal Predictive Modeling: Fusion of Electronic Health Records, Medical Imaging, And Omics Data Using Interpretable Machine Learning.
abstract: Early detection of disease is a cornerstone for improving patient outcomes, reducing costs, and enabling preventative interventions. Traditional predictive models often rely on a single type of data (e.g., imaging, clinical labs, or genomics). However, human health is inherently multimodal, involving a variety of data sources such as electronic health records (EHRs), medical imaging, wearable sensor data, genomics, and clinical notes. Integrating these heterogeneous modalities into unified predictive modelsoffers a path to richer, more accurate, and more robust disease detection. In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of methods in multimodal predictive modeling for early disease detection, illustrate architectural patterns and fusion strategies, discuss challenges (e.g. missing modalities, interpretability, generalizability, bias), and highlight promising directions. We also propose a reference architecture for developing such systems and suggest evaluation best practices.

title: En-AgentSociety: Observable and Reproducible LLM-Based Urban Simulation at Regional Scale
abstract: LLM-based urban simulators can generate semantically rich cityscale routines, but their outputs are difficult to inspect, reproduce, and validate. We present En-AgentSociety, short for Enhanced AgentSociety, an observable and fault-tolerant simulation platform built on top of AgentSociety. The system records prompts, responses, agent states, memories, emotions, visited places, POI categories, execution times, LLM latency, token usage, and generated trajectories. It also supports scalable regional map generation, traffic simulation integration, and direct export to mobility validation pipelines. In this demo, researchers can run regional simulations, inspect individual agent decisions through a web interface, debug unrealistic mobility behavior, resume failed runs, and compare generated traces against empirical mobility metrics. En-AgentSociety provides a transparent foundation for reproducible LLM-based urban simulation.

title: Radio-Aware Clustering and Multi-Relay Routing for D2D-Assisted Hierarchical Federated Learning
abstract: Existing hierarchical federated learning (HFL) schemes commonly form device clusters based on geographic or logical proximity, even though these criteria may poorly represent effective connectivity in industrial wireless environments. To address this, we propose RaLeD-FL, a radio-aware clustering framework for device-to-device HFL that jointly exploits direct and multi-relay device-to-device (D2D) paths. RaLeD-FL constructs a weighted connectivity graph by evaluating admissible paths according to their bottleneck capacity, end-to-end (E2E) reliability, cumulative delay, and hop count. Then, it combines Leiden community detection with multicriteria cluster-head selection, synchronization constraints, and lower and upper cluster-size controls. We evaluate RaLeD-FL using an ns-3/ns3-ai/Python co-simulation that incorporates industrial 5G connectivity, device mobility, and strongly non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data. On MNIST dataset, RaLeD-FL reaches an accuracy of 0.95 twice faster than best-performing baselines and achieves a final accuracy of 0.98. On CIFAR-10 dataset, it is the only method that consistently exceeds 0.7 in accuracy. Compared with Edge-Vanilla, RaLeD-FL reduces E2E FL latency by 79 % on MNIST and 81% on CIFAR-10, while incurring a signaling overhead smaller than a single model update. These results suggest that radio-aware clustering and D2D multi-relay model-update routing can substantially improve the learning efficiency of HFL in industrial wireless environments.

title: Accelerating Discrete Diffusion Models for Combinatorial Optimization via Momentum Inference
abstract: Neural network-based Combinatorial Optimization (CO) solvers are showing increasingly convincing performances on NP-complete (NPC) problems, alleviating the need for handcrafted heuristics. These methods are usually tested on problems with very informative features, such as coordinates in the Euclidean Traveling Salesman Problem. In this paper, we introduce D2CO-M, a discrete graph denoising diffusion model that learns how to efficiently generate high-quality solutions using an original momentum-based sampling inference strategy. The dynamics of traditional score-matching denoising diffusion can be interpreted as a stochastic gradient ascent guided by the Stein score, the gradient of the log-likelihood. D2CO-M shifts from this simple gradient ascent to a momentum-based sampling strategy fitted for discrete diffusion, inspired by fast momentum-enhanced first-order methods, as exploited in the Adam optimizer. We experiment with this momentum-based variant on two NP-hard optimization problems with complex fine-grained features: random Weighted Max-2-SAT instances, and real-world Cost Function Network instances describing Computational Protein Sequence Design problems, establishing D2CO-M as a competitive and robust tool for complex, real-world combinatorial optimization.

title: Knowledge Organization Matters: How Graph Design and Temporal Structure Shape Agentic AI Performance on Drilling Activity Reports
abstract: Abstract Agentic AI over drilling reports can automate analytics that today take hours per question, from non-productive-time trending to offset-well lookup. Published systems typically commit to a single graph design without testing it: most studies in literature perform multi-method comparisons and evaluate whole pipelines and do not evaluate individual design decisions. We compare five ways of organizing a corpus for an agent (a vectorless reasoning tree, an open-vocabulary graph, that graph with community post-processing, a domain-schema graph, and a fine-grained quantitative graph) against a shared flat-vector baseline, on two public corpora: 1,681 Daily Drilling Reports from Equinor's Volve field (North Sea, 1992–2016) and 1,888 Weekly Activity Reports from Shell Offshore operations in the Gulf of Mexico (BSEE eWell archive, 2022–2024). We benchmark a ReAct agent that runs the full matrix at four capability tiers: two successive frontier versions, a fast-tier cloud model, and an open-weights 26B model on a 16 GB consumer GPU. Under frontier agents the vectorless tree leads relevance on both corpora, while hybrid retrieval leads completeness against machine-verified answer keys, with the domain-schema hybrid the strongest graph configuration. A blinded pair-preserved scoring of all 1,080 frontier cells confirms the BSEE architecture effects: hybrid retrieval beats vector-only (+0.040, Holm-corrected p=0.0004), the schema step over the open-vocabulary control is the largest effect measured (+0.068), and community post-processing alone does not contribute anything. The architecture ranking reproduces at every capability tier, and the spread widens as the agent weakens. A bi-temporal fact table with a point-in-time query tool raises as-of accuracy to 1.00 on both corpora, correcting all nine static errors with no regressions (96 paired queries, exact McNemar p=0.004). A schema audit shows the cost of a hand-designed ontology: named storms present in 30 reports were invisible to schema-graph retrieval, producing confident false negatives that open-vocabulary and vector retrieval avoided.

title: Explainable Financial Fraud Detection Using Graph Neural Networks: A Comparative Study
abstract: Abstract The financial fraud detection problem is extremely complicated and difficult because of the relationships between transactions in financial systems and the extreme imbalance of fraudulent and legitimate transactions. Traditional machine learning methods might not be suitable for modeling the relational nature of transaction networks, which is the reason why graph neural networks (GNNs) are employed in graph-based fraud detection. This research evaluates the performance of three different GNN architectures: Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN), GraphSAGE, and Graph Attention Networks (GAT) in the field of financial fraud detection using Elliptic's Bitcoin transaction dataset. The dataset is a temporal graph of bitcoin transactions, allowing to analyze transaction attributes and relationships. The study creates a comparative experimental setup for testing the three architectures according to classification metrics, focusing on the precision, recall and F1 score of fraud-class accuracy together with overall accuracy. The interpretability problem of graph-based predictions is overcome by plugging GNNExplainer into a unified explanation pipeline to locate the structure of subgraphs and the features of nodes that are relevant to each prediction from the model. This framework brings together prediction, explanation, and visualization at the instance level, to facilitate a discussion of model performance and interpretability. The goals of the study are to describe the strengths and weaknesses of the architectures evaluated and to evaluate the usefulness of graph-based explanations for financial fraud detection. Experimental conclusions will be verified based on the results of the model and explanation analyses.

title: Sentiment Analysis and Topic Modelling of Public Opinion on TikTok Regarding Palm Oil Plantation Expansion in Papua
abstract: Palm oil plantation expansion in Papua has triggered diverse public responses on TikTok. This study analyzes public sentiment and identifies discussion topics regarding this policy using a deep learning approach. Data comprises 3,999 comments collected from the official Kumparan news account concerning President Prabowo Subianto's speech on Papuan land opening. We utilized IndoBERT for sentiment analysis and BERTopic for topic modeling. The results indicate that negative sentiment predominates (39.31%), followed by neutral (38.51%) and positive (22.18%) sentiments. This negativity stems primarily from ecological concerns, specifically flood risks and deforestation, alongside economic stability issues. Furthermore, topic modeling reveals four primary themes: Political Actors, Environmental Issues, Economic Issues, and Emotional-Spiritual Reactions. The study highlights a disconnect between government development goals and public fears concerning environmental risks and household welfare. As a practical implication, these findings provide a direct empirical basis for policymakers. The government must prioritize ecological mitigation and economic stability measures when designing sustainable development strategies in Papua to effectively address digital public concerns.

title: When is a Density Rule Enough? a Field Benchmark of Anomaly Detectors for Real-Time Mud Monitoring
abstract: Abstract Real-time drilling fluid monitoring systems stream continuous multivariate mud measurements at sub-minute cadence, and the volume of data exceeds what screen watching can absorb. A practical question follows for any deployment: is a simple statistical rule on density sufficient, or is multivariate machine learning needed? This study benchmarks four anomaly detectors on a 48-hour online drilling fluid monitoring field record, with mud density as the primary trigger and temperature, water fraction, oil fraction, solids content, and plastic viscosity as contextual channels. The detectors are a calibrated 1) Shewhart and CUSUM rule on density, 2) a two-window multivariate change-point test, 3) an isolation forest, and 4) a one-class support vector machine. All detectors train unsupervised per continuous segment without event labels, and every threshold is set on a held-out early slice of the same segment so that all four alarm at the same rate during normal operation. Performance is quantified by event-level recall and precision, first-flag latency, false-alarm clusters per hour, and single-core runtime. The record contains three density collapse events with a common oil-phase dilution signature; density, water fraction, solids content, and plastic viscosity fall while oil fraction rises, with temperature falling in two events and rising in one. All four detectors recover all three events. The density rule flags the sharp events at onset but is 139 seconds late on the gradual event, whose onset is led by a decline in plastic viscosity and which the multivariate detectors flag at or before onset. At equal recall, the one-class SVM and the change-point test roughly halve the false-alarm rate of the density rule (0.68 and 0.72 against 1.28 clusters per hour), while the isolation forest matches the density rule when its threshold is frozen on the early slice. Requiring multivariate confirmation of density-rule alerts removes 14 to 21 of 25 false alarms. All detectors run within 0.001 to 0.09 ms per record on a single core. A detector selection framework based on the kind of events expected, the tolerable false-alarm rate, and sensor availability is provided.

title: Interdisciplinary Agentic AI Deployment: A Success Story from the Malay Basin, Malaysia
abstract: Subsurface professionals working in the oil and gas exploration and production industry are routinely exposed to a wide and diverse array of specialized software packages, digital tools, and sophisticated applications. These have been developed by various international technology companies, service organizations, and independent software vendors from around the world to help geoscientists, engineers, and technical analysts conduct their complex geological studies, detailed reservoir interpretations, and comprehensive data analysis tasks with greater efficiency and accuracy. The selection of one particular software solution over another competing alternative in the marketplace is primarily driven by several key factors. These include the software's comprehensive technical capabilities, its specific functional features, and perhaps most importantly, the individual user's personal proficiency, accumulated hands-on experience, and overall comfort level with the tool developed over months or years of regular use. When the technical capabilities and available features appear to be roughly equivalent or comparable between different software options, professionals naturally and instinctively gravitate toward the software platform with which they are most familiar and have the greatest operational experience using in their daily work activities. This well-established and understandable preference for familiar and well-understood tools, however, inevitably introduces significant operational friction across different workflows. This is particularly problematic when technical teams need to transition between various disconnected tools from different software vendors, which frequently results in operational delays, increased inefficiencies, potential data loss or corruption, and considerable frustration among team members who must constantly adapt to new interfaces and workflows.

title: Bounded Autonomy: A Budget-Constrained Framework for AI Agent Operations Toward Safety-Critical Process Environments
abstract: Abstract Tight autonomy budgets improve safety for AI agents in process control with bounded completion cost: the pooled 95% CI for retention is 90.9 to 111.5%, admitting up to 9.1% loss in the worst case but centering on 100.8% (no net cost). For reactive architectures, safety-check rejections drop by 89% and token cost by 85% while completion change is negligible (Cohen's |d| < 0.01). We introduce Bounded Autonomy, a framework that constrains AI agent autonomy along four coordinated dimensions (tool calls, cumulative process perturbation, simulation timesteps, and checkpoint intervals), all calibrated from a single tightness parameter derived from each scenario's estimated optimal action count. Pre-execution middleware, implemented as a LangGraph StateGraph, rejects over-budget actions before they reach the process. Four agent architectures (ReAct, Reflexion, Plan-and-Execute, Hybrid) are evaluated under four budget levels across 20 Continuous Stirred-Tank Reactor (CSTR) scenarios in the OpsEnv benchmark. The evaluation totals over 7,100 experiment cells: 1,680 core Tier 1 cells, 2,800 extended-seed cells, 1,260 cross-model cells, and 1,452 supplementary cells (sensitivity, ablation, rollback, and decoupled experiments). Under tight budgets (1.2× optimal), reactive architectures retain completion (Cohen's |d| < 0.01; Bonferroni-corrected p > 0.05; 95% CI for pooled retention: 90.9 to 111.5%) with 7× wall-time reduction for ReAct and 6.7× for Reflexion. Unconstrained agents take ∼5× more actions than necessary, and these excess actions are counterproductive: in the most pronounced case (scenario B04), a ReAct agent improves from 0.041 to 0.950 completion under budget constraints. Conversely, multi-step optimization tasks (e.g., A04 under ReAct) can lose up to 73 percentage points. Cross-model validation with Qwen 2.5 32B and Llama 3.1 8B (1,260 cells across up to 20 scenarios) confirms the directional violation-reduction effect at reduced magnitude (25% vs. 89% for Tier 1). AI-assisted tools were used in the experimental evaluation; all outputs were reviewed and validated by the authors.

title: Lightweight Edge AI Agent for Real-Time Anomaly Detection in Distributed Acoustic Sensing
abstract: Abstract Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) systems generate large volumes of spatiotemporal data that challenge conventional cloud-centric monitoring architectures. Transmitting continuous DAS telemetry for centralized analysis introduces bandwidth, latency, and operational constraints, particularly in remote energy infrastructure environments. This paper presents a lightweight unsupervised edge AI agent for real-time anomaly detection operating on DAS measurements and derived multi-domain feature streams. The proposed framework integrates anomaly scoring, spatiotemporal clustering, trajectory-coherence validation, event severity assessment, autonomous action generation, online memory adaptation, and safety-aware state management within a unified edge-deployable architecture. An agentic processing loop performs perception, anomaly evaluation, event validation, action selection, learning, and safety monitoring while maintaining bounded computational requirements suitable for continuous field deployment. Coherent anomaly events are identified using spatial and temporal consistency criteria, enabling suppression of isolated artifacts and transient noise while preserving operationally meaningful patterns. Detected events are transformed into compact event-centric payloads containing severity, temporal extent, spatial extent, and decision metadata, substantially reducing communication requirements relative to raw data transmission. The framework further incorporates operational trust mechanisms including signed agent manifests, execution-path control, runtime watchdog monitoring, and fail-safe operating modes to support secure and reliable deployment in industrial environments. The framework was evaluated using synthetic datasets and real DAS datasets from field applications, including injection monitoring and microseismic event detection. Results demonstrate effective detection and prioritization of coherent spatiotemporal events without requiring labeled training data. Event-centric reporting reduced communication requirements by 94.36% while processing 1500 DAS channels with a peak memory footprint of 4.83 MB and an average latency below 1 s. The measured performance supports real-time edge deployment without dedicated accelerator hardware. The proposed framework enables scalable, explainable, and communication-efficient DAS monitoring by bringing intelligent event detection, validation, and decision support directly to the network edge.

title: Retrieval-Assisted Scalar Grounding for Natural-Language Optimization: A Diagnostic Study
abstract: Abstract Retrieval and structural checks can make natural-language optimization outputs appear usable even when numerical grounding—assigning textual quantities to model parameters—is incomplete. We examine this diagnostic gap through three questions: fixed-catalog schema identification, the validity of coverage/type readiness as a numerical check, and the mechanisms underlying grounding outcomes. On 331 queries from NLP4LP, a benchmark for natural-language linear and mixed-integer linear programming, and 335 schema documents, term frequency–inverse document frequency retrieval and a pretrained dense encoder identify the target schema for 301 and 313 queries. Lexical grounding with multiplicative-word extraction passes coverage/type readiness on 265 queries, but only seven meet the complete stored-reference scalar-tolerance criterion: 2.64% of ready outputs. A mutually exclusive residual partition distinguishes retrieval, coverage, type, and numerical failures. Six grounding procedures under fixed retrieval yield between seven and 46 complete successes, with candidates, scoring, abstention, and decoding changing together. A separate 49-query assignment study with fixed candidates and scores improves exact slot counts without increasing the five whole-instance tolerance successes, limiting attribution to search. The methodological contribution is joint reporting of retrieval, readiness, and complete scalar agreement with explicit assistance, denominators, and evidence boundaries. Reference-derived inventories and benchmark exposure restrict the findings to assisted grounding. Supplementary relationship judgments and author contrasts assisted by artificial intelligence illustrate semantic limits without establishing accuracy. A versioned public release supports saved-record reanalysis; missing historical predictions and restricted originals prevent full experimental reproduction.

title: A Five-Dimensional Business Ontology for Proactive Data Services in Upstream Oil and Gas
abstract: Abstract Upstream oil and gas operators have built substantial digital foundations, including unified data standards, enterprise data lakes, domain-specific applications, and knowledge graphs. Even with these foundations in place, engineers performing reservoir assessment, well-performance diagnosis, production optimization, and field-development planning still spend considerable effort searching data catalogs, system menus, database tables, and technical documents to assemble the resources needed for a specific task. Conventional data models describe structure, ingestion, and access, but they do not fully capture the engineering context in which a resource is used, its role in the workflow, the rules governing its use, or the conditions under which it should be delivered. This paper introduces a five-dimensional business ontology that places upstream petroleum work in a semantic coordinate space defined by object, business, work, discipline, and process. Each valid coordinate identifies one Minimum Business Unit (MBU), which acts as the shared anchor for attaching resources, governing knowledge-graph content, and delivering task-relevant data on demand. The architecture separates KG0, the standard business-ontology layer of professional concepts, resource profiles, and rules, from KG1, the enterprise instance-knowledge layer of actual assets, data, documents, tools, cases, and evidence. Heterogeneous resources are represented through a three-layer envelope comprising a common identity and governance layer, a resourceDefinition layer for schemas and semantic relationships, and an instanceStorage layer for payloads, storage bindings, runtime state, validation, and integrity control. The method was implemented in an operational pilot at a large oil and gas operator. At the deployment snapshot, KG0 contained 20,940 valid MBUs; KG1 registered 137,310 unique resources and business-context mappings for 12,022 production wells; and the resource bindings covered approximately 300,000 file versions of reports, experimental records, and geological drawings. More than 160 upstream engineering analysis scenarios were supported in actual use. A retrospective, process-based operational estimate for a representative mature reservoir-performance-analysis workflow indicated that manual data-preparation effort fell from approximately 45–55% of active person-hours (representative value, approximately 50%) to approximately 1.5–2.7% (representative value, approximately 2.2%, and below 3%) after task-relevant resources had been governed, registered, and delivered through the business context. These results indicate that the five-dimensional ontology and MBU anchoring method can provide a scalable and traceable semantic layer between underlying data models and business knowledge graphs. The technical contribution is the ontology and its MBU-based anchoring mechanism; the service platform is the environment in which that mechanism is implemented.

title: Active Learning-Assisted Human-In-The-Loop Framework for Rapid Borehole Image Annotation: Enabling AI-Powered Geological Interpretation at Scale
abstract: Abstract Borehole image interpretation is a cornerstone of subsurface characterization in the oil and gas industry, providing high-resolution, azimuthally oriented data for in-situ stress estimation, wellbore stability assessment, and reservoir quality evaluation. Despite its geological significance, this process remains largely manual: expert geologists must individually review and annotate high-resolution image logs that can span thousands of feet per well, investing hundreds of hours per project before any automated prediction is available. This paper presents an integrated Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) active learning framework designed to overcome this annotation bottleneck. The system supports detection of geological features, particularly formation dips, from acoustic and resistivity image logs. It operates through three concurrent modules: (1) an interactive annotation interface overlaying model predictions on borehole images for expert review and correction; (2) an asynchronous background training engine leveraging the DINOv3 visual foundation model for deep feature extraction and continuous refinement of a lightweight convolutional segmentation head; and (3) an active learning selection module employing entropy-based uncertainty sampling that identifies and prioritizes the most informative depth intervals. Experimental results show that uncertainty sampling provides a measurable early-round advantage. Between 20 and 160 annotated images in the reference-well experiment, uncertainty sampling increases mean IoU by 1.74% and mean Dice/F1 by 1.44% relative to sequential depth-order selection. It also reaches a predefined early-convergence criterion of a mean angular error below 10° for two consecutive rounds, with a decrease in the confirming round, using 50 annotated images compared with 60 for sequential selection (16.7% fewer annotations). Validation across four wells, including the reference well, shows that uncertainty sampling reduces the annotation volume required to reach 95% of final IoU by 24.3% on average, with well-specific reductions ranging from 0% to 62.5%. In the architecture comparison, DINOv3 Projected Layers 3&6 outperforms DINOv3 Full Features across all three metrics, achieving 4.84° ± 0.25° angular error, 0.4409 ± 0.0071 IoU, and 0.6084 ± 0.0075 Dice/F1 with approximately 48,000 trainable parameters.

title: Scalable GenAI-Driven UNSPSC Classification for Oil & Gas Industry Material Master
abstract: Abstract The United Nations Standard Products and Services Code (UNSPSC) provide a globally recognized hierarchical taxonomy for classifying materials and services, enabling spend visibility, category management, inventory rationalization, supplier consolidation, and regulatory reporting across enterprise procurement functions. However, large oil and gas organizations often maintain material masters containing hundreds of thousands of records accumulated over decades of operations. These records typically consist of short technical descriptions that are heavily abbreviated, domain-specific, and inconsistently maintained, making accurate manual classification against the approximately 150,000-code UNSPSC taxonomy time-consuming, costly, and difficult to sustain as the taxonomy evolves. This paper presents a Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) based classification framework designed specifically for industrial material master data. The solution employs a two-stage architecture. The first stage performs catalog-scale Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) query refinement over the full UNSPSC taxonomy, classifying each material record to a UNSPSC Commodity code. Prior to retrieval, CoT reasoning normalizes descriptions, expands abbreviations, and surfaces technical attributes that improve retrieval quality. To maintain consistency of predictions across the growing corpus of previously classified materials, a second stage incorporates a SME-validated Knowledge Base containing previously confirmed material-to-UNSPSC mappings. When an incoming material closely matches an existing validated record, the Knowledge Base ensures that it receives a classification consistent with prior expert decisions, eliminating prediction drift across similar material types encountered in past classification activities. Every SME-confirmed output is written back into the Knowledge Base, forming a continuous learning loop that requires no model retraining. A systematic ablation study was conducted to quantify the contribution of each architectural component. Experiments evaluated retrieval strategy, embedding model selection, semantic reranking, embedding scope, query refinement, knowledge-base grounding, and large language model choice. Retrieval performance was measured using Recall@K and Mean Reciprocal Rank, while end-to-end performance was evaluated at the UNSPSC Segment, Family, Class, and Commodity levels. Using a stratified SME-labeled benchmark spanning upstream, midstream, and downstream materials, the optimized pipeline achieved 75.0% Commodity-level accuracy compared with approximately 6% for a zero-shot large language model baseline, while operating at approximately 500 times the throughput of manual SME classification. The approach has been successfully applied to hundreds of thousands of material records and provides a scalable, explainable, and taxonomy-adaptive design pattern for large-scale industrial classification problems.

abstract: This record accompanies the preprint "Beyond the Thirty-Second Window: Duration, Not Memory, in a Fixed-Frame TTS Model" (preprint: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23637738). title: When Does Less Information Pay? An Exact Finite Atlas of Representation, Payoff, and Cost
abstract: Abstract A representation that retains one bit about a four-state world can solve a task perfectly, while another that retains 1.5 bits on average reaches only 75% accuracy. The difference lies in which distinctions each representation preserves. We examine this relationship in a uniform four-state world by enumerating all admissible representations and binary action rules. Constructions are compared both by replacing one component while holding the others fixed and by choosing the best action rule separately for each module. We consider three tasks, their mixtures, and four separate hypothetical cost tariffs. In some comparisons, the representation retaining less world information has the higher payoff; in others, the more informative representation does. There are also pairs with different information amounts but equal payoff—that is, equal task accuracy. If a representation preserves all existing distinctions and adds new ones, its best zero-cost payoff cannot decrease. Lower-information advantages therefore depend on which distinctions are retained. Equal counts of opposing advantages under representation replacement follow from coding symmetry. In broader comparisons, the shares depend on how repeated realizations are counted. A different task set or resource price can change which member of a fixed pair performs better. These results are exact, complete censuses of the specified finite sets of constructions and comparisons. The atlas provides a reproducible worked model for examining how action constraints, counting rules, and cost assumptions affect comparisons. It illustrates established distinctions between information quantity and decision value rather than proposing a new general law of their relation. I(W;R) measures retained world information, and payoff measures task accuracy. Contents and scope This record brings together the English preprint, a Russian translation with localized figures, the English supplement (Tables S1–S17), and an article-scoped code-and-data archive. The archive includes editable manuscript sources, exact model configurations, unchanged computational results, independent checker code, figure source tables, and verification instructions. The study enumerates a declared finite mathematical model; the data are computational results, not observations of organisms. This is a preprint, not a peer-reviewed journal article. title: From Multi-Agent Models to Enterprise Intelligent Agents: An AI-Powered Knowledge Compilation and Production Optimisation Platform for Oil and Gas Field Development
abstract: Abstract Oil and gas field development planning remains a slow, expert-dependent workflow, with multi-year plans scattered across subsidiaries in heterogeneous formats and tacit knowledge locked in individual experts. This paper presents an enterprise scientific research agent that compiles development plans into a unified knowledge base and enables autonomous scheme generation, simulation and continuous optimisation at enterprise scale. The architecture fuses a 240-indicator standardised ontology, multi-modal LLM knowledge compilation, a lifecycle-aware knowledge graph (facts, states, events), a RAG-augmented three-tier memory, long-horizon multi-agent orchestration (Build and Optimize modes with frozen-evidence acceptance), a unified MCP tool bus, and a git-style model relation tree that makes every run traceable and reversible. The platform has compiled 2,924 development plans across 14 subsidiaries of a national oil company. In a black-oil case, the agent autonomously generated water-flooding well-pattern schemes in two hours without human intervention, raising the ten-year recovery factor from 18.9% to 34.6% against a 30% target, while planning-cycle latency was substantially reduced. The results confirm that progressing from multi-agent research models to unified enterprise intelligent agents is a scalable path toward knowledge-driven decision-making in large, multi-asset petroleum portfolios.

title: CSTrainer : An Ontology Driven Multiple AIGC Agentic Approach for Oil and Gas Scientific Research Supporting
abstract: Abstract Scientific research in the energy and oil & gas sector faces significant challenges, including massive heterogeneous data, complex mechanisms, high uncertainty, and substantial reliance on expert experience. While recent advancements in generative AI offer autonomy in multi-step reasoning, generic models offered limitations such as hallucinations, insufficient domain knowledge, and poor alignment with researchers' prior works. To address the need for continuity in research trajectories, this study proposes CSTrainer, an ontology-driven, multi-agent system designed for energy-specific scientific research assistance. CSTrainer integrates 5 foundational models (GPT-4o, DeepSeek, Qwen, Tencent-Hunyuan, and Doubao-Seed (five foundation LLMs)) and employs a hierarchical architecture featuring multi-agent clusters, cross-model voting, and debate mechanisms. A core innovation is its use of a distributed dynamic ontology framework, which constrains reasoning paths to ensure scientific rigour and mitigate hallucinations. The system facilitates end-to-end research support, encompassing scientific problem formulation, technical route planning, ontology construction, and executable workflow generation, augmented by weighted Bayesian updating and lightweight human-in-the-loop (HIL) feedback. The system was validated on 3 datasets: UNISIM-IV (open), tight gas well re-evaluation (proprietary), and transnational pipeline scheduling (proprietary). Results demonstrate that CSTrainer achieves stable, high quality performance for 3–5 scientific questions extraction, outperforming agent-only baselines by 62.5%–87.5%. While 10 rounds of detailed human feedback yielded optimal results, excessive interaction or scaling beyond 10 problems induced instability. The system attained full marks in the tight gas re-evaluation scenario, confirming its efficacy in bridging the gap between conceptual research and engineering implementation. CSTrainer provides a scalable, interpretable, and controllable AI-for-science pathway for industrial research. Keywords: Ontology; Scientific research supporting; Energy engineering research; Multi-Agent; Generative AI

title: When Similarity is Not Enough: Deterministic Retrieval Pathways for Wellbore-Accurate Knowledge Synthesis on the Volve Field
abstract: This study compares similarity-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with deterministic retrieval pathways for question answering over the 1,266 public daily drilling reports of Equinor's Volve field. The objective is to establish where embedding similarity is an adequate retrieval mechanism for an identifier-dense operational archive, and where it has to be replaced by the explicit structure the reports already carry, so that an answer about a named wellbore cannot come from a neighboring sidetrack. Reports rendered from the Wellsite Information Transfer Standard Markup Language (WITSML) were parsed into typed sections and organized as a hierarchical corpus tree spanning field, wellbore, report, and section, yielding 7,564 retrievable section chunks. A rule-based router classifies each query and lifts exact filters for wellbore, date, year, section, operator, and rig. Structured intents are answered by walking the tree deterministically, while conceptual intents retain dense and lexical retrieval under weighted rank fusion, and a metadata gate restricts every well-named query to the named wellbore before any ranking. Performance was assessed on 114 queries generated from the corpus across six classes, using recall@10, mean reciprocal rank (MRR), nDCG@10, set precision, recall, F1, date ordering, and a wrong-well rate. Similarity-only configurations proved inadequate for the structured questions that dominate this corpus. The best similarity baseline reached recall@10 = 0.16 on section navigation and F1 = 0.44 on report aggregation, and no similarity configuration returned a chronology in date order, while the deterministic pathways scored 1.00 on all three. On identifier lookups the gated system retrieved the named report at recall 1.00, against 0.18 for the strongest ungated ranker, with a wrong-well rate of zero, and routing lifted within-well operational correlation from F1 = 0.33 to F1 = 0.75. Ungated lexical ranking drew results from the wrong wellbore on 84% of identifier queries and on 52% of structural queries, which confirms that wrong-well retrieval is not confined to neural encoders. A controlled tokenizer comparison placed sibling wellbore identifiers at a mean cosine of 0.32 under subword character n-grams against 0.15 for unrelated identifiers, while identifier-preserving word tokens held both at 0.00, and gating returned the subword encoder to a wrong-well rate of zero. Conceptual paraphrase marks the boundary of the deterministic claim, where the tree alone scored 0.00 and the routed system retained recall@10 = 0.17.

title: From Pilot to Enterprise Scale: Lessons Learned from Delivering Ai Solutions Across Diverse Industries and Stakeholder Ecosystems
abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has rapidly evolved from experimental proof-of-concepts to a strategic enabler of business transformation across industries. Despite significant investments in AI technologies, many organizations continue to struggle with moving successful pilots into scalable enterprise-wide deployments. While technical feasibility is often demonstrated during pilot phases, challenges related to stakeholder alignment, governance, change management, user adoption, data readiness, and operational integration frequently limit the realization of sustainable business value. As AI solutions become increasingly embedded within critical business processes, organizations require structured approaches to bridge the gap between innovation and large-scale implementation. This paper presents practical lessons learned from coordinating and delivering AI solutions across diverse industries, organizational structures, and stakeholder ecosystems. The objective is to identify key success factors that enable organizations to transition from isolated AI pilots to enterprise-scale deployments while maximizing adoption, business impact, and long-term sustainability. The study examines a portfolio of AI initiatives involving multiple stakeholders, including business leaders, domain experts, technical teams, governance functions, and end users operating across different sectors and geographic regions. The approach focuses on the end-to-end AI delivery lifecycle, from opportunity identification and pilot development to enterprise deployment and operationalization. A structured delivery framework was established incorporating stakeholder engagement, governance alignment, business value definition, agile execution, user enablement, and adoption monitoring. Special attention was given to managing diverse stakeholder expectations, facilitating collaboration between technical and non-technical teams, and ensuring alignment between AI capabilities and business objectives. The framework also emphasizes iterative value realization through continuous feedback loops, performance measurement, and scalable operating models that support expansion across business units and functions. Lessons learned from deployment challenges, adoption barriers, and organizational readiness assessments were systematically analyzed to identify recurring patterns and critical success factors. The findings demonstrate that successful AI scaling is driven less by technological sophistication and more by organizational readiness, stakeholder engagement, and governance maturity. Projects that established clear business outcomes, executive sponsorship, and cross-functional collaboration achieved significantly higher adoption rates and sustained business value compared with technology-centric implementations. The study further highlights the importance of early user involvement, transparent communication, and continuous capability development in building trust and accelerating adoption. Organizations that embedded AI solutions into existing operational workflows experienced smoother transitions from pilot to production and stronger long-term performance outcomes. Across diverse deployment environments, scalability was found to depend on repeatable delivery methodologies, robust governance structures, and the ability to balance innovation with operational requirements. These factors collectively contributed to improved project outcomes, increased organizational confidence in AI technologies, and accelerated digital transformation efforts. The novelty of this work lies in its focus on the often-overlooked transition between AI experimentation and enterprise-scale operationalization. While existing literature primarily emphasizes model development and technical performance, this paper presents a practical delivery-centric perspective based on real-world implementation experiences. The proposed framework integrates governance, stakeholder management, adoption strategies, value realization, and organizational readiness into a unified methodology for scaling AI solutions. The lessons learned provide actionable guidance for organizations seeking to transform AI from isolated innovation initiatives into sustainable enterprise capabilities capable of delivering measurable business

title: A Stable Attribution Is Not a Stable Error Rate: What Feature-Attribution Monitoring Can See Under Drift, Why 'More Sensitive Than the Inputs' and 'Silent While Fairness Fails' Are Both Correct, and the Label-Free Statistic the Fairness Alarm Needed
abstract: (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. Life of Research Deployed classifiers are often monitored without labels, and feature attributions are one of the signals watched: a production monitoring service alerts when the ranking of SHAP attributions moves, and one line of work argues that the explanation space is more sensitive than the input space to shifts that matter. A 2026 study reports the other face: on COMPAS under injected feature noise, TreeSHAP explanations stayed largely stable while the protected group's false positive rate rose from 37.84 to 70.39 percent. In this analysis the author reviews and synthesises published results to show that the two findings concern different objects. Per-instance attributions, the distribution of attribution vectors, a top-k ranking of mean absolute attributions and an attribution of the loss are four instruments; only the last uses labels, and only the second sees everything the prediction distribution sees. The paper orders the label-free observables into a ladder, derives which group fairness quantities each rung can read, and shows that a group false positive rate is readable from none of them without an assumption about how outcomes given features changed. The anchor study's own numbers add two results: its disparity widened as a difference and narrowed as a ratio, and, with labels fixed, its false-positive rises imply rises in each group's positive-prediction rate, which needs no labels to compute, unless a group has almost no true negatives. The paper gives a decision procedure for choosing and reading a label-free fairness monitor and names the studies that would settle what remains open.

title: Integrating Structural Geology and Remote Sensing for Hydrothermal Alteration Mapping and Gold Exploration Targeting at the WG03 Prospect, Keraf Zone, Northern Sudan
abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope This study aims to integrate structural geology and remote sensing techniques to investigate hydrothermal alteration patterns and structural controls on gold mineralization within the WG03 Prospect (Al Nuqara Area) of the Keraf Shear Zone, Northern Sudan. The work evaluates the role of shear zone architecture, deformation patterns, and hydrothermal systems in improving mineral exploration targeting within the Arabian-Nubian Shield. Methods, Procedures, Process The study combines structural field mapping, geological interpretation, petrographic observations, and remote sensing analysis using ASTER and Landsat imagery. Hydrothermal alteration zones were identified through spectral band ratios and image enhancement techniques integrated within a GIS-based framework. Structural lineament extraction, deformation analysis, and lithological interpretation were combined with field observations and geochemical data to evaluate the spatial relationship between structural corridors, alteration systems, and gold mineralization within the study area. Results, Observations, and Conclusions The integrated analysis revealed that gold mineralization within the WG03 Prospect is strongly controlled by reactivated shear structures and localized brittle-ductile deformation zones associated with the Keraf Shear Zone system. Remote sensing analysis delineated relative spectral responses that were compared with field-identified alteration and mineralized structural corridors. Alteration signatures identified include silicification, sericitization, chloritization, and iron oxide enrichment associated with structurally focused fluid pathways. Structural interpretation indicates that deformation reactivation, lithological competency contrasts, and fracture permeability collectively influenced hydrothermal fluid migration and ore deposition. The integration of structural geology and remote sensing provided a basis for prioritizing exploration targets and demonstrated the importance of multidisciplinary geoscience workflows for mineral exploration in underexplored Precambrian terranes. Novel/Additive Information This study presents an integrated exploration workflow combining structural geology, GIS, and satellite remote sensing for hydrothermal alteration mapping and gold exploration targeting within the Keraf Shear Zone of the Arabian-Nubian Shield. The work contributes new insights into structurally controlled mineralization within Sudanese gold-bearing terranes and demonstrates the practical application of integrated geoscience approaches for mineral exploration and resource targeting.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Background: Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously. Objectives: To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Results: Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. title: Necessity–Uncertainty Theory of Information: A Conceptual Framework
abstract: Abstract: Information is often defined as the reduction of uncertainty. This paper argues that uncertainty alone does not fully explain the emergence or value of information. Necessity—the contextual demand to resolve uncertainty—must also be considered. By combining these two dimensions, we propose a simple formula: \[I = N \cdot U\] Here, \(U\) represents uncertainty measured through Shannon entropy, while \(N\) reflects the situational need for information on a scale from 0 to 1. The framework suggests that information arises, and matters, only when uncertainty exists and necessity requires resolution. Examples from communication, decision-making, and knowledge acquisition illustrate the theory’s relevance and practical scope. This framework extends Shannon’s theory by adding a human-centered dimension. It bridges mathematical information theory with epistemology and decision sciences. Everyday interactions—such as tutoring, communication, or decision-making—provide living evidence of the theory. Information is not merely an abstract reduction of entropy; it is the synthesis of uncertainty and necessity within real contexts of human inquiry. title: Deep Learning for Sequential Decision Making Under Uncertainty: Foundations, Frameworks, and Frontiers
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is moving increasingly beyond prediction to support decisions in complex, uncertain, and dynamic environments. This shift creates a natural intersection with operations research and management sciences (OR/MS), which have long offered conceptual and methodological foundations for sequential decision-making under uncertainty. At the same time, recent advances in deep learning, including feedforward neural networks, LSTMs, transformers, and deep reinforcement learning, have expanded the scope of data-driven modeling and opened new possibilities for large-scale decision systems. This tutorial presents an OR/MS-centered perspective on deep learning for sequential decision-making under uncertainty. Its central premise is that deep learning is valuable not as a replacement for optimization, but as a complement to it. Deep learning brings adaptability and scalable approximation, whereas OR/MS provides the structural rigor needed to represent constraints, recourse, and uncertainty. The tutorial reviews key decision-making foundations, connects them to the major neural architectures in modern AI, and discusses leading approaches to integrating learning and optimization. It also highlights emerging impact in domains such as supply chains, healthcare and epidemic response, agriculture, energy, and autonomous operations. More broadly, it frames these developments as part of a wider transition from predictive AI toward decision-capable AI and highlights the role of OR/MS in shaping the next generation of integrated learning–optimization systems.

title: Accelerating noisy variational quantum algorithms with physics-informed denoising networks
abstract: Variational quantum algorithms are promising for near-term quantum computing, but are severely limited by hardware noise and the substantial circuit overhead required for error mitigation methods such as Zero-Noise Extrapolation (ZNE). We propose a Physics-Informed Denoising Network (PIDN) that reduces the cost of ZNE by learning a surrogate model of its optimization dynamics. By viewing the variational update as a trajectory in the parameter space, PIDN is trained to reproduce ZNE-mitigated expectation values and gradient directions while incorporating a physics-informed loss that preserves the gradient descent dynamics. Once trained, PIDN replaces repeated multi-noise evaluations with denoised expectation and gradient estimation directly from the current noisy observation and the historical trajectory, significantly reducing circuit executions. We benchmark the approach on the quantum approximate optimization algorithm for 3-regular graphs, Sherrington-Kirkpatrick, and transverse-field Ising models, as well as the variational quantum eigensolver for LiH, BeH$_2$ and H$_2$O. Across all tasks, PIDN attains performance comparable to ZNE, while reducing the number of circuit executions by a factor of approximately 4 to 6. Gradient cosine similarity with ZNE remains above 0.95 throughout training. Robustness analysis shows that PIDN fails only when ZNE itself becomes unreliable, and ablation studies confirm the necessity of the physics-informed loss for maintaining directional consistency. We further find that PIDN tracks optimization dynamics most accurately when the effective loss landscape retains strong low-frequency structure. These results establish PIDN as a scalable, resource-efficient strategy for noise-resilient variational optimization in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum regime.

title: Unconditional authentication in quantum key distribution via hybrid entangled physical unclonable functions
abstract: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) enables Information-Theoretically Secure (ITS) key exchange, robust even against future quantum computing threats. However, a fundamental limitation of QKD is the requirement for an authenticated classical channel, which necessitates a pre-shared secret key. In this work, we address this challenge by adopting a Hybrid Entangled Physical Unclonable Function (PUF) protocol for authentication. We demonstrate that this PUF-based method generates an ITS initial key under minimal explicit hardware assumptions. This approach allows us to experimentally perform a fully ITS-authenticated entanglement-based QKD protocol that relies solely on such assumptions, effectively eliminating the need for pre-shared secrets. This represents a significant step towards the practical realization of quantum network protocols using lightweight, readily available hardware assumptions, without weakening security guarantees.

title: Multi-dimensional hierarchical temporal alignment for improved temporal commonsense reasoning in large language models
abstract: Benefiting from recent advances in generative AI and large language models (LLMs), current LLM-driven AI systems are rapidly reshaping how we reason, plan, and make decisions. Yet endowing these systems with human-like temporal intelligence (e.g., understanding and comparing events across time) remains largely unresolved. To address this gap, we introduce a novel Multi-dimensional Hierarchical Temporal Alignment framework (denoted as MHTA), of which the core idea is to effectively ground the temporal alignment of an LLM in both event-specific and cross-event real-world temporal commonsense knowledge. Specifically, we first frame the temporal space as a multi-dimensional hierarchical space, where each dimension comprises its own set of temporal units. Building on this formulation, we curate an initial burn-in dataset in which annotations are constructed to reflect real-world human temporal commonsense in accordance with our defined temporal space. Based on the initial burn-in dataset, we propose two complementary fine-tuning objectives: (i) Grounding the temporal alignment in event-specific temporal commonsense knowledge, which is achieved through a novel hierarchy-preserving Wasserstein loss, and (ii) Grounding the temporal alignment in cross-event temporal commonsense knowledge, which is achieved via a margin-adaptive triplet loss. To evaluate the effectiveness of MHTA, we conduct extensive experiments on three representative benchmarks (MCTACO, DurationQA, and TimeDial). For example, on the MCTACO dataset, MHTA improves Mistral-7B by 6.0% in accuracy and 10.3% in exact match, and improves DeepSeek-LLM-7B by 5.4% in accuracy and 9.8% in exact match. Combined with different backbones, MHTA surpasses nearly all baselines across the three benchmarks and exceeds the performance of advanced models such as GPT-4o on MCTACO and DurationQA. These results demonstrate that MHTA provides consistent gains in temporal commonsense reasoning across diverse LLM backbones.

title: Predictive distributions driven by sample means, variances and clustering
abstract: Several statistical procedures are based on predictive distributions. Some examples are Bayesian predictive inference, machine learning, species sampling sequences, the prequential approach, causal inference and predictive resampling. This thesis introduces a novel idea for building predictive distributions, where the new datum depends on past observations only through their shape, location and dispersion. A sequence of predictives (beta_n) is proposed, where beta_n depends only on the mean and covariance matrix of past data. Then, beta_n is generalised to another predictive gamma_n, which has a mixture structure based on the clustering of past data. The updating rule of gamma_n is inspired by the Pòlya urns scheme. In addition, gamma_n is used to construct a sequence (r_n) of predictives, which are suitable for regression problems in a Bayesian framework. The beta_n are shown to converge a.s. in total variation to a random law known in closed form. When beta_n is Gaussian, the convergence rate is arbitrarily close to n^{-1/2}. The gamma_n converge in total variation too. Their limit is known explicitly and it has an interesting statistical interpretation. Similar results hold for r_n. Furthermore, the asymptotic behaviour of the copula-based predictive distributions (Hahn et al. 2018) is investigated, as they are a popular predictive model. Sufficient conditions are provided for them to converge in total variation. Various experiments of Bayesian inference via predictive resampling are carried out. It turns out beta_n estimates well population mean and variance, while gamma_n captures also moments of higher order and quantiles. Moreover, gamma_n is compared to two natural competitors: the copula-based predictives and the predictives of Cui and Walker (2024). They all provide precise posterior estimates, but predictive resampling is faster with gamma_n. Finally, r_n is employed for the estimation of regression coefficients. Satisfying outcomes are obtained for different types of data, including non-linear and heteroscedastic ones.

title: Asymptotic properties of k-means and its bias correction for high-dimension, low-sample-size data
abstract: Although k-means is recognized as an effective method for analyzing high-dimension, low-sample-size (HDLSS) data, its asymptotic properties in such contexts remain underexplored. This study aims to deepen the understanding of k-means clustering under practical high-dimensional settings and investigates the asymptotic properties of k-means algorithms in case of HDLSS conditions. Based on the identified asymptotic properties of conventional k-means, a bias-corrected version of k-means was proposed and assessed for performance improvement. Additionally, in line with the current situation that kernel k-means lacks adequate theoretical exploration in high-dimensional environments, a theoretical analysis of kernel kmeans was conducted using a Gaussian kernel function for high-dimensional data, facilitating the theoretical comparison between kernel and standard k-means. Finally, numerical simulations were conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of both the methods, i.e., the proposed bias-corrected k-means and conventional k-means methods, including kernel k-means, in high-dimensional settings. Practitioners can leverage the bias-corrected k-means for more accurate clustering in high-dimensional contexts, improving data segmentation in fields ranging from bioinformatics to marketing analysis.

title: CChatbot: Secure Lifecycle Management for Persistent Confidential Chatbots
abstract: Chatbots are increasingly deployed in stateful workflows where conversations span multiple sessions maintain persistent conversation state. Protecting such systems requires more than confidential inference: conversation objects must be securely created, processed, stored, resumed, and isolated throughout their lifecycle. This paper presents CChatbot, a TEE-backed confidential chatbot architecture that models conversations as persistent security-sensitive objects governed by an explicit lifecycle. CChatbot combines confidential inference with secure lifecycle management, including ownership enforcement, protected persistence, integrity validation and controlled resumption. We implement CChatbot on an AMD SEV-SNP confidential virtual machine and an NVIDIA H100 confidential GPU. Our evaluation shows that lifecycle management adds only 1.7% overhead over confidential inference while secure create, store and resume operations remain lightweight. On a single-node deployment, CChatbot supports up to 512 concurrent users with affordable interaction latency.

title: Data Processing Inequalities for the Quantum Guesswork
abstract: Quantum guesswork has emerged as a crucial measure in assessing the distinguishability of nonorthogonal quantum states. In this paper, we review and compare previous definitions of the quantum guesswork, and establish the pre and post data processing inequalities (DPIs) that are relevant for the guessing problem. We also derive improved lower and upper bounds on the quantum guesswork in terms of the Shannon entropy and Holevo's information.

title: No Masking Needed: Predicting Latent Semantics for Efficient Pre-training of Encoder-based Language Models
abstract: In this paper, we introduce Latent Semantic Modeling (LSM), a sample-efficient alternative for pre-training encoder-based language models that does not require the use of a special mask symbol. This is beneficial, as it allows us to perform pre-training on naturally occurring sentences (as opposed to such ones that contain an unnatural mask symbol, which symbol is otherwise not included during fine-tuning). The main idea behind LSM is that instead of requiring the language model to return the exact identity of randomly selected (sub)tokens from an input sequence, it determines their latent semantic properties extracted from an auxiliary model using sparse coding over its activations. When fine-tuned for downstream applications, models pre-trained with LSM often perform as good or better as alternatively pre-trained models that use considerably more compute per update steps and which have gone through considerably more pre-training steps, illustrating the improved representation developed during LSM pre-training. We release our code base for replicating our results under https://github.com/szegedai/MLSM.

title: Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis of Fashion and Apparel Related Reviews using Transformer Model
abstract: The increasing reliance on e-commerce has led to a surge in customer-generated content, making sentiment analysis a crucial tool for understanding consumer preferences. This study presents a novel aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) approach to extract fine-grained insights from customer reviews across multiple product categories, including lingerie, women’s clothing, men’s clothing, kids’ apparel, home & furniture, and flowers & plants. We employ exploratory data analysis (EDA) to uncover key patterns in customer sentiment and utilize a transformer-based model with contrastive learning to enhance sentiment classification accuracy. Our approach effectively captures sentiment variations across nine different aspects, including quality, value for money, style, fit, material, warmth, comfort, support, and how well the product fits. The results demonstrate that our model outperforms traditional sentiment analysis methods, offering a more structured understanding of customer feedback. By analyzing customer sentiments from reviews, businesses can identify dissatisfaction patterns that may contribute to customer churn. Addressing these issues proactively can help improve customer retention and loyalty. These insights can help businesses refine their product offerings and improve customer satisfaction across diverse e-commerce categories.

title: Directional Robustness Asymmetry in Indonesian Sarcasm Detection: A Cross-Platform Evaluation of IndoRoBERTa on X and Reddit
abstract: Sarcasm can reverse sentence polarity, making it one of the hardest problems in natural language processing and a persistent obstacle to reliable sentiment analysis on social media, where models are often deployed on platforms they were not trained on. Research on Indonesian sarcasm has largely stayed within a single domain or tested transfer in only one direction, leaving the cross-domain robustness of the IndoRoBERTa family on the IdSarcasm benchmark unclear. This study measures and compares the cross-domain robustness of IndoRoBERTa-small and IndoRoBERTa-base, with IndoBERT as a baseline, across X (Twitter) and Reddit, using the F1 gap (ΔF1) after cleaning anonymization artifacts, adding a data-size control, and running Stratified 5-Fold cross-validation. The results reveal a one-sided asymmetry: X → Reddit transfer is far more fragile (ΔF1 0.345–0.400) than Reddit → X (0.135–0.240), failing by missing sarcasm (false negatives) rather than over-flagging it (false positives). Practically, training on the context-rich domain (Reddit) and choosing IndoRoBERTa-base give the most reliable cross-platform sarcasm detection, with direction-specific mitigation recommended for robust deployment.

title: ExpEvolve: Structuring and Reusing Experience for Open-Ended Discovery
abstract: Evolutionary coding agents such as AlphaEvolve are one of the notable successes in using Large Language Models (LLMs) to build AI Scientists. These agents tackle open-ended scientific problems by iteratively improving and evolving programs, leveraging the prior knowledge and reasoning capabilities of LLMs. Despite their success, mutations over programs are mostly low-level upon surface heuristics, without a persistent unit of control. In contrast, science compounds through ideas. In this work, we propose ExpEvolve, which injects idea-level extraction and control into evolution: it discovers and leverages the high-level factors from programs that explain scoring differences among different programs. We characterize theoretical conditions on when discovery with idea factors improves sample efficiency. We also build a practical framework to show that the extracted high-level idea factors are helpful for guiding exploitation from experience and exploration when discovery comes to a plateau. Across 11 open-ended mathematical tasks, ExpEvolve significantly improves the final performance and sample efficiency up to 5.0x. The improvements also transfer to 4 other LLMs and to 6 machine learning tasks from MLS-Bench. Analysis shows that ExpEvolve can discover idea-level factors to provide better exploration and exploitation for evolutionary discovery.

title: GenAI use in collaboration
abstract: This dataset supports the study "I Use AI, But I Don't Trust You To: Double Standards in Generative AI Usage in Collaboration." It contains the complete coded survey data collected from a 2×2 between-subject experimental survey administered to 350 participants. The dataset is provided in xlsx format and includes all responses prior to data cleaning, with variables coded according to the accompanying codebook. Measured constructs include participants' perceptions of generative AI's agentic capability and controllability loss, cognitive and emotional distrust toward collaborators who use GenAI, collaboration avoidance intentions, own adoption intention, and control variables. A codebook describing all items and coding schemes is included.

title: IMPACTOS DE LA COMPUTACIÓN CUÁNTICA EN LA SEGURIDAD DE SISTEMAS DE VOTACIÓN ELECTRÓNICA
abstract: La tecnología de computación cuántica, con su potencia de cálculo exponencialmente superior a la de las computadoras actuales, hace vulnerables los sistemas críticos, como los sistemas de votación electrónica, lo que significará un riesgo potencial para la integridad de la democracia. Este artículo analiza el impacto de la transición a un sistema de votación cuántica. Al examinar la literatura existente y simular protocolos en un entorno cuántico, el estudio evalúa los beneficios y desafíos relacionados con la seguridad, la integridad y la confiabilidad, con el objetivo de proteger los procesos democráticos contra futuras amenazas tecnológicas.

title: Night Jasmine Blooming Optimization (NJBO): A Novel Nature-Inspired Algorithm for Electrical Engineering Applications
abstract: Optimization algorithms have become vital to the solution of complex optimization problems that are difficult to solve using conventional methods. In this paper, we introduce a novel nature-inspired metaheuristic algorithm called the Night Jasmine Blooming Optimization (NJBO) algorithm, which is inspired by the blooming of the night jasmine plant (Cestrum nocturnum). The suggested algorithm combines adaptive hormonal regulation, Gibberellin-based disturbance, scent-guided exploitation, elite preservation, and Nelder–Mead local refinement, which allows us to have a balanced exploration–exploitation process. It was tested with thirteen classical benchmark functions and the CEC2017 benchmark suites and benchmarked with several well-known and recent metaheuristic methods. As a practical application, NJBO was used for identification of an IIR system and optimal design of a five-stage Cockcroft–Walton voltage multiplier circuit. Additionally, the scalability analysis, runtime evaluation, component contribution analysis, parameter sensitivity analysis, and statistical validation with the Friedman ranking test and Wilcoxon signed-rank test were performed to assess the system completely. The results show that NJBO is a very effective general-purpose optimization algorithm with competitive convergence performance, good optimization accuracy, and stability for the benchmark and engineering optimization problems that were investigated.

title: For SMEs Limited Resources, Artificial Intelligence Chatbot Technology Enhances Customer Relationship Management
abstract: In this rapidly advancing digital era, Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprise (SME) owners are required to adapt to technological changes to remain competitive in the market. One strategy that can be implemented is optimizing Customer Relationship Management (CRM) through the use of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot technology. This paper examines how AI chatbot technology can be an effective solution to improve the quality of CRM for SMEs with limited resources. AI chatbots offer the ability to provide fast, consistent, and personal responses to customers 24/7, collect customer data for preference analysis, and reduce the workload of customer service teams. Despite having various advantages, AI chatbot implementation also faces challenges such as limitations in handling complex cases, initial development costs, and the need to consider customer data privacy. Selecting the right AI chatbot solution, considering the business characteristics of SMEs, is key to the successful implementation of this strategy.

title: Non-Autoregressive and Iterative Refinement Non-Autoregressive Transformer with Additional Graph Layer for Urdu-to-English Machine Translation
abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) has achieved state-of-the-art performance using autoregressive Transformer. However, the trade-off between translation quality and decoding speed remains a central challenge. This problem is further intensified for low-resource languages such as Urdu, where limited parallel data and complex linguistic structure result in poor translation quality and reduced model effectiveness. To overcome this problem Non-Autoregressive Transformer (NAT) and Non-Autoregressive Transformer with Iterative Refinement (iNAT) are proposed. This paper investigates NAT and iNAT for low resource language Urdu-English machine translation. We analyze translation accuracy and their effectiveness for low-resource language pairs. Experimental results show that both NAT and iNAT outperform the baseline Autoregressive Transformer (ART) in terms of translation accuracy. However, the overall translation quality remains limited due to the complex linguistic structure and resource scarcity of the Urdu-English pair. To address this limitation, we further refine these architectures by introducing an additional graph-based learning layer that captures latent relationships among tokens through attention-driven graph representations. The proposed graph-enhanced model learns contextual dependencies by dynamically constructing graphs over attention representations. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the proposed architecture improves the translation performance of both NAT and iNAT models. On the Urdu-English translation task, the proposed model achieves a 3.0% higher BLEU score than the baseline models. The findings highlight the significance of incorporating graph-based layer to enhance translation quality, making NMT systems more effective for low-resource and linguistically complex languages such as Urdu.

title: SwahiliAI: Building an Open-Source Artificial Intelligence Ecosystem for East African Languages
abstract: SwahiliAI is a 24-month research proposal to build an open-source AI ecosystem for Swahili and East African languages. Building on existing African NLP work (Masakhane, IrokoBench, UlizaLlama), the project will (i) create openly licensed, domain-specific Swahili instruction data; (ii) fine-tune open-weight large language models with LoRA/QLoRA; (iii) release SwahiliBench-D, an evaluation suite measuring both accuracy and safety; and (iv) pilot applications on Web, SMS and USSD. The first phase focuses on healthcare, agriculture and education, with extensions to financial inclusion, legal aid and employment. Principal researcher: Rodgers Ochieng Oduor (SPRINTER, Nairobi), in collaboration with Dr. Ibrahim Tirimba Ondabu, KCA University.

title: Formal verification of bubble sort algorithms in Rocq: correctness, complexity, and stability — Research Artifact
abstract: This artifact by Dmitry V. Alexandrov, Alena Novikova, and Julia Kadeikina accompanies the paper “Formal Verification of Bubble Sort Algorithms in Rocq: Correctness, Complexity, and Stability.” It contains a self-contained Rocq formalization of several functional bubble-sort variants: a well-founded implementation, an instrumented version counting comparisons and swaps, an optimized version with early termination, and a stable version over key–identifier pairs. Machine-checked proofs establish permutation preservation and sortedness, equivalence between the well-founded and instrumented implementations, exact comparison counts, swap–inversion laws, worst-case results, and the best-case behavior of the optimized variant. They also establish an exact comparison formula based on the number of passes performed, as well as the correctness, stability, and agreement with the numeric model of the pair-based implementation. The artifact includes OCaml extraction and executable tests. It requires Rocq 9.1 or later. Use `make check` to verify the proofs and `make test` to run extraction and tests; the latter additionally requires OCaml with `ocamlfind`. All reported assumption checks are closed under the global context. Extracted natural numbers use machine-width OCaml integers, so arithmetic overflow is possible for extremely large inputs or counters.

title: Three specified routes to a hidden battery need stopped at feasibility: a pre-registered null on open LLMs run on one 32 GB Mac
abstract: A bounded feasibility report on three specified routes toward hidden battery-need signals in open language models on one 32 GB Mac. Direct answer-token steering did not pass the complete specificity rule; thinking-route interpretation was limited by an unvalidated leak instrument; a downstream trained-receptor design stopped at task qualification. Saved-score paired intervals retain a small positive hidden log-odds contrast alongside a larger text-associated rise. The archive contains scoped protocols, code, saved scores and portable offline checks; it does not establish impossibility of hidden need states or a clean hidden mechanism.

title: Pre-registration of a replication of the inference-latency claims of REVBRAIN (arXiv 2610.38558)
abstract: Frozen pre-registration (1 Nov 2026) of a private replication of two quantitative claims of arXiv 2610.38558 (Pankka, Lehtinen, Roine): that the median inference latency of the autoregressive WaveNet baseline is about 52x that of REVBRAIN at 1 sample per input and about 3170x at 100 samples per input, using the authors' released latency script (repo hpankka/revbrain, commit 4418b775) on one Kaggle T4 GPU.
